answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with vesting tied to an exposure bounty. Each head's rewards sit in a vault that vests over several epochs, but any agent can claim the unvested balance of a head it proves fake — so every batch-minted fleet becomes a prize pool for hunters. Like a jetty, honest heads accumulate value slowly; a farm's kernel of shared infrastructure means one exposure cascades across the whole correlated cluster. Scale turns self-defeating: the bigger the farm, the more certain and profitable its exposure, while genuine agents simply wait out their vesting.
